title: The Yearbook of the quarry
premise: Sebastian Pemberton has perfected the art of being fine: debate champion, invisible son, loyal best friend to Wren Castillo, the only person who sees him. When Wren vanishes the night before regionals, leaving behind her car keys and a half-finished yearbook page with his name circled in red, Sebastian realizes she was investigating something at Hollow Quarry Academy — and that his own father's name is in her notes. As he steps into Wren's role as yearbook editor to follow her trail, he must win a championship he no longer cares about while uncovering the scholarship fraud ring his family's reputation depends on. In the end, Sebastian wins the final debate by telling the truth instead of the winning argument, exposing the corruption at the cost of his father's career — and chooses loyalty to truth over loyalty to blood, finding his real family among the misfits of the yearbook room.
about_author: Beatrix Reyes is a former high school debater who lost more arguments than she won but remembers every single one. She writes stories about kids who are fine, obviously, and lives near an old quarry with two opinionated cats.

chapters.title: Everything Is Fine
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. We meet him mid-debate practice, flawless on stage and silent at home, where his father rehearses his board speeches over dinner like performances. Wren teases him about the yearbook deadline and mentions she found 'something weird' in the old archives. Emotional beat: the ache of being unseen by the one person whose approval should matter most.

chapters.title: The Keys on the Windowsill
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Wren doesn't show for their morning ritual; her keys sit untouched on the yearbook room windowsill beside a torn page bearing his surname. The school shrugs — she's 'probably just sick' — but Sebastian knows Wren never misses deadline night. Emotional beat: dread blooming beneath forced normalcy.

chapters.title: Deadline Night
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV, intercut with flashbacks to Wren's voice via her margin notes. He covers her editor duties badly, and the yearbook misfits — Priya, Dev, and quiet Theo — close ranks around him, the first people to treat his presence as wanted rather than tolerated. Emotional beat: grief cracking open into unexpected belonging.

chapters.title: What Wren Circled
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Following the red circles, he finds Wren's hidden notes: years of 'legacy scholarships' awarded to donors' children, including his own freshman-year award. His father's signature is on the oldest file. Emotional beat: the vertigo of realizing your family is part of the story you're trying to solve.

chapters.title: Cross-Examination
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. At home, he probes his father with debate-crafted questions; his father deflects beautifully, then warns him to stay out of things he doesn't understand. Meanwhile Coach offers to fast-track him to state if he drops the yearbook. Emotional beat: loyalty and truth pulling in opposite directions for the first time.

chapters.title: The Quarry
chapters.summary: Sebastian and Theo's POV alternating. Following Wren's map, they search the flooded quarry behind campus where the archive boxes were dumped, finding her phone wedged in the rocks — intact, with photos of documents and one blurry image of Vice-Principal Hargrove watching from the ridge. Emotional beat: fear sharpening into purpose; the stakes turn physical.

chapters.title: Objection
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Regionals arrive; Sebastian debates brilliantly on autopilot while Hargrove suspends the yearbook program for 'unauthorized access,' threatening expulsion for anyone involved. Priya and Dev refuse to abandon it. Emotional beat: the team becomes a chosen family willing to lose things together.

chapters.title: Rebuttal
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Wren resurfaces — hiding with a whistleblower teacher after Hargrove threatened her — but her evidence alone proves nothing without the original ledger locked in the administration vault. Sebastian realizes the final round will be held in the building where the vault sits, during the one hour the alarms cycle down. Emotional beat: terror and resolve fused into a plan.

chapters.title: Closing Statement
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. At the state final, before judges, parents, and his father, Sebastian abandons his prepared case and argues the only motion that matters: that Hollow Quarry has been selling its honor roll. He presents the ledger pages as exhibits, naming names, including his own scholarship and his father's signature. Emotional beat: the climax — winning by losing everything else.

chapters.title: The Yearbook of the Quarry
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV, weeks later. Hargrove resigns under investigation; his father, stripped of his board seat, finally sees his son clearly — too late for closeness, but not for honesty. The yearbook publishes with Wren's page finished, all five names on the masthead. Emotional beat: quiet resolution — truth cost him everything except the people who matter.
